channel.title: AI Changelog
channel.description: New AI and data science papers, repos, models, tools and news.

item.title: [news] GPT-6.1 Terra
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement.

item.title: [news] Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model (155 responses)
item.description: Trending on Hacker News from blog.cloudflare.com. 102 points and 33 comments.

item.title: [paper] Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
item.description: While language models have become dramatically more capable, retrieval still largely relies on lexical matching or similarity in fixed embedding spaces. This creates a capability asymmetry: what the retriever fails to find, even the strongest generator cannot recover.

item.title: [paper] Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies
item.description: Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. This update is usually presented as an estimate of a smoothed gradient.

item.title: [paper] Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
item.description: As autonomous research systems become more capable, benchmarks must both evaluate their performance and support meaningful research progress.

item.title: [paper] VibeVideoBench:Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
item.description: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a ruleconsistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events.

item.title: [paper] Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
item.description: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone.

item.title: [paper] Do vision models know that three is three?
item.description: Do vision models encode the transition $2{\to}3$ the same way whether it appears in handwritten digits or in hand gestures, and do they "understand" that clean${\to}$dirty is the same transformation regardless of whether it is applied to a kitchen or a carpet?

item.title: [paper] On the stability of learning
item.description: Learning algorithms are usually analyzed under the assumption that informative gradients are continuously available.

item.title: [paper] FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
item.description: 4D novel view synthesis (NVS) aims to render dynamic scenes across viewpoints and timestamps, which requires jointly inferring 3D structure and temporal dynamics.

item.title: [paper] OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
item.description: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control.

item.title: [paper] Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) show promise in specialty medicine, yet existing evaluations largely focus on isolated clinical encounters rather than tracking how clinical responsibilities evolve across a longitudinal care pathway.

item.title: [paper] Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
item.description: Expanding multilingual ASR systems to new languages is challenging when adaptation must preserve previously supported languages without replaying source-language training data.

item.title: [paper] Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
item.description: The paper proposes a unified framework for work agents that integrates foundation models with runtime harnesses to execute complex digital tasks reliably, introducing dimensions of persistence and openness alongside capability families and evaluation metrics.

item.title: [paper] MedVTok: A General-Purpose Medical Visual Tokenizer
item.description: Multimodal medical AI requires a common visual interface for encoding heterogeneous imaging evidence for patient condition modeling.

item.title: [paper] ACARE: Agent-Context-Aware Reranker for Iterative Search
item.description: In agentic search, a document can match an agent-generated sub-query without helping answer the user's original question. Conventional rerankers score documents against the sub-query alone, overlooking the broader task and the agent's reasoning.

item.title: [paper] I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
item.description: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent. AI agents' increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly.

item.title: [paper] Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
item.description: In federated learning (FL), secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of local model updates of $N$ clients, without revealing any information on the individual model updates to the server, beyond their sum.

item.title: [paper] Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
item.description: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be…

item.title: [paper] Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
item.description: A vulnerability costs more to fix the later it is discovered. As coding agents generate code faster than developers can review it, software needs a first line of defense screening each new function in real time.

item.title: [paper] Seeing Through Distractions: Context-Stable Attribution via the Least Core
item.description: Shapley-value-based explanations are widely used for feature attribution in machine learning. However, in computer vision, a feature may reduce the target-class score when added to the complete genuine image, even when the predicted label remains unchanged.

item.title: [paper] Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?
item.description: Selection bias in large language models (LLMs) can persist despite instructions to ignore presentation order or prompts that elicit reasoning.

item.title: [paper] Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
item.description: Browser agents do not just need more practice. They need to practice the right things. We introduce MiniWeb, a realistic miniature of the web comprising 65 interconnected websites across 15 domains, where agents navigate, search, and transact as people do.

item.title: [paper] Recertifying decisions via e-closure: uniform improvements of conformal risk control and randomized e-BH
item.description: Statistical procedures often control expected loss at a prescribed level while leaving part of their risk budget unused.

item.title: [paper] Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
item.description: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task.

item.title: [paper] Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation
item.description: Editing multi-camera concerts requires coordinated decisions about musical relevance, visual quality and cut timing.

item.title: [paper] Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
item.description: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one.

item.title: [paper] Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
item.description: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response.

item.title: [paper] Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
item.description: Many academic disciplines (in particular, mathematics and the theoretical sciences) face difficult questions about how to adapt their practices to the rise of highly capable artificial intelligence (AI).

item.title: [paper] FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
item.description: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions.

item.title: [paper] Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
item.description: Deep research, or any use of large language models (LLMs) to read a large document collection and produce insights, requires synthesizing information from different sources.

item.title: [paper] Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
item.description: Preference optimization can learn spurious correlations, and augmenting the preference data with ties (equally preferred responses) can reduce spurious reliance. However, ties differ in their corrective effect, making their selection for augmentation important.

item.title: [paper] A theory of noisy linear recurrent neural network learning dynamics
item.description: Biological neural networks are noisy: their dynamics involve difficult-to-predict fluctuations which are likely due not just to chaos, but also to a variety of low-level biophysical processes.

item.title: [paper] Atomic Security Concerns: Towards a Foundational Language for Security Knowledge Representation
item.description: Cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and security architecture rely on numerous concepts, including security properties, domains, controls, risks, implementation measures, capabilities, and compliance requirements.

item.title: [paper] A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
item.description: Interactive environments offer a practical way to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents, and competitive games extend this evaluation to decisions shaped by competing goals and other agents' choices.

item.title: [paper] Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
item.description: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents.

item.title: [paper] Improving Signals, Declining Encoder: A Known-Answer Test of Label-Free Monitoring in Self-Supervised Learning
item.description: Self-supervised training is monitored without labels, through the loss and statistics of the learned features. We report a case where we know the encoders lost part of what they had learned, so we can check whether these signals noticed.

item.title: [paper] Do Similarity Measures Measure Similarity? How User Activity Creates Phantom Correlation in Recommender Systems
item.description: Item-item similarity is one of the oldest and most foundational signals in recommender systems: two items are assumed to be similar when the same users consume them.

item.title: [paper] Beyond Physical Illness: Can Clinical Narratives Reveal Emerging Mental Health Risks in Chronically Ill Patients?
item.description: Mental-health risks such as depression, dementia, and suicidal ideation can emerge during hospitalization among chronically ill patients and may worsen without timely recognition and intervention.

item.title: [paper] EEGaze: Multimodal Attention Prediction in Visual Search via EEG-Based Saliency Refinement
item.description: Visual search is ubiquitous in daily life, from locating keys in a messy apartment to finding a tool in a cluttered workshop or an application icon on a desktop screen.

item.title: [paper] VidEdit3D: Flexible 3D Gaussian Editing with Video Diffusion
item.description: Recent advancements in text-guided 3D editing, particularly with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown promise but still lag behind the flexibility of 2D editing tools.

item.title: [paper] CLOSURE: Cross-Channel Closure for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
item.description: Multivariate time series produced by industrial installations and server clusters are under continuous monitoring, and anomaly detection is the first line of defense before a local fault escalates into a system-wide failure.

item.title: [paper] Model Selection for Off-Policy Evaluation via Pairwise Bellman Validation
item.description: Model selection and hyperparameter tuning pose a central challenge in off-policy evaluation (OPE) because errors of fitted Q-functions and occupancy-ratio estimates cannot be directly evaluated from held-out transitions.

item.title: [paper] SEMA-Auto: Sighted and Efficient Multi-Turn Attack with Autonomy
item.description: Existing jailbreak attackers fall into two classes: static planners fix their single- or multi-turn adversarial plans in advance, remaining simple but losing sight of the victim's replies, wasting turns and limiting transferability; interactive generators read each victim reply…

item.title: [paper] LUCID: Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with Conditional Density Estimation
item.description: Computing local-level variable importance (VI) is critical for understanding machine learning models. Local permutation-based VI metrics offer a simple yet powerful approach, measuring how much a model's output changes when perturbing its inputs.

item.title: [paper] Preference-Guided Cooperation in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning (MOMARL) addresses agent coordination and objective trade-offs simultaneously while optimising overall system performance.

item.title: [paper] Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
item.description: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control.

item.title: [paper] A Category-Selective Encryption Framework for Privacy Protection of UAV Images
item.description: Imagery captured by unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems increasingly raises privacy concerns, as UAV aerial surveillance routinely captures sensitive objects such as pedestrians and vehicles alongside ordinary scene content.

item.title: [paper] TRACE: Memory-Efficient Time Series Class-Incremental Learning via Temporal-Spectral Reconstruction
item.description: Web-connected sensing applications continuously generate multivariate time series with evolving behavioral categories, making Time Series Class-Incremental Learning (TSCIL) essential for adapting to new classes without forgetting previously acquired knowledge.

item.title: [paper] The Watchtower Imperative: Lifespan-Calibrated Evaluation for Frontier AI
item.description: The gap between AI capability deployment and safety assurance is structural and cannot be closed through internal evaluations alone.

item.title: [paper] MatAnyone-E: Sparse Memory Propagation for Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting
item.description: High-resolution video matting requires preserving fine details, such as hair strands and soft transparency, while maintaining consistency across frames.

item.title: [paper] Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
item.description: Clinical trial prescreening requires distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient records.

item.title: [paper] Quantifying the failure of symmetry learning in linear diffusion models due to initialization and finite-sample effects
item.description: Data distributions often possess one or more symmetries: for example, all orientations of any specific dog are included in the distribution of all possible dog pictures.

item.title: [paper] Audit Where Hacks Pay: Budgeted Strong-Verifier Audits Against Reward Hacking in GRPO
item.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains on cheap checks, such as unit tests, that a policy can learn to game, while a stronger check is too expensive to run on every rollout.

item.title: [paper] Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
item.description: Transformer-based language models exhibit an astonishing capacity to generalize to longer and more difficult problem instances than those seen in training. However, theoretical understanding of this phenomenon still lags behind.

item.title: [paper] Detecting bus delays and service anomalies in Niterói with autoencoder latent feature representations
item.description: Bus riders judge service by two failures: single trips that run late, and days on which the whole system misbehaves. We ask whether one unsupervised representation of raw GPS telemetry can serve both diagnoses on the NetMob 2026 Niterói bus dataset.

item.title: [paper] Triage: Skip, Skim, or Refine Attention Tiles in Video Diffusion Transformers
item.description: Attention over tens of thousands of visual tokens dominates the inference of video diffusion transformers (DiTs). Existing methods reduce this cost through sparsity, low precision, or both, but use a single precision for all kept tiles.

item.title: [paper] Explainable Multimodal AI Approach to Reduce Unnecessary Breast Biopsies
item.description: Recently, there has been rise in multimodal vision-language models for computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), yet their application in breast diagnosis, particularly for predicting biopsy outcomes remains limited.

item.title: [paper] From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
item.description: For large language models (LLMs) and multimodal large language models (MLLMs), model-reported self-confidence is often miscalibrated, yet it may still be useful for efficient evaluation.

item.title: [paper] MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors
item.description: Error-targeted learning gives a legible way to improve a model: identify specific weaknesses of the model, train the model to fix these weaknesses, and check whether the weaknesses are fixed.

item.title: [paper] Towards a Unified Framework of Optimal Input-Side Dimensional Configuration for Deep CTR Prediction
item.description: Deep click-through rate (CTR) prediction has achieved substantial success through increasingly expressive feature interaction architectures. However, predictive performance also depends on how input-side information is configured before interaction modeling.

item.title: [paper] Not One Belief: Answer Payloads, Persistence, and Dissociated Confidence Signals in Conversational Question Answering
item.description: Conversational QA systems should fix errors when users push back and signal which answers to trust.

item.title: [paper] GNN-VIEW: Visual Inspection and Explanation of Graph-based Earth-System Models
item.description: Machine learning Earth-system models are becoming increasingly important, and so is their development. Graph-based models, one of the most prominent approaches, allow developers to constrain the learning process before training via graph connectivity.

item.title: [paper] EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
item.description: Serving web queries at scale with multi-agent systems requires jointly configuring large language models, collaboration modes, agent counts, interaction rounds, and skills.

item.title: [paper] TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
item.description: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in high-level reasoning and task planning for robots. However, specialized domains remain a challenge for VLMs' image interpretation and grounding abilities.

item.title: [paper] Adapting LLM-SC to Living Sacred Heritage: Domain-Specific Extraction, Semantic Networks and Human Evaluation on Pashupatinath Temple Reviews
item.description: Large language model (LLM) pipelines can turn visitor reviews into structured data, but generic schemes may miss rituals, sacred spaces, cultural restrictions and emotionally mixed experiences at living sacred heritage sites.

item.title: [paper] OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
item.description: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input.

item.title: [paper] Printed and Scanned: Exposing the Fragility of Single-Image Morphing Attack Detectors under Print-Scan Degradation
item.description: Face morphing attacks, in which the biometric traits of two or more identities are blended into a single face image, pose a severe threat to identity document issuance and automated border control.

item.title: [paper] CounterFlow: Target-Conditioned Flow Matching for Visual Counterfactuals
item.description: In eXplainable AI, counterfactual explanations have gained significant traction by offering users direct, intuitive, and actionable insights into model decisions.

item.title: [news] webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox
item.description: Research: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs console.log() to standard…

item.title: [paper] Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks
item.description: As frontier language models grow increasingly capable and autonomous, independent third-party evaluations are critical for characterizing their systemic safety risks.

item.title: [paper] SCAFFOLD under Hessian Similarity: Sharp Convergence Rates
item.description: One of the main challenges of federated learning is heterogeneous data split among the clients, leading to biased local updates called client drift.

item.title: [paper] A Hybrid Framework for Explainable Aviation Risk: Causal Chain Extraction from Safety Reports with Physics-Based Failure Quantification and Interventional Analysis
item.description: Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. Computational work on these archives has mostly sorted reports into fixed taxonomies.

item.title: [paper] Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms based on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) are vulnerable to sim-to-real gaps.

item.title: [paper] Improving JEV Entailment Reranking with Span Readouts and Selective Adaptation
item.description: JEV decision models pair a language model backbone with a lightweight scoring head to select among natural-language options.

item.title: [paper] Active Learning of Conditional Generative Models via the Transport Neural Tangent Kernel
item.description: Many high-throughput scientific experiments produce distributional outputs, requiring conditional generative models to interpret the data, and to predict outcomes at new inputs.

item.title: [paper] TRON: Transferring Naturally Evolved Network Architectures into Neuroevolution
item.description: Neural architecture search (NAS) is challenging because of the vast, non-linear space of artificial neural network (ANN) topologies.

item.title: [paper] Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
item.description: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron.

item.title: [paper] VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
item.description: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM).

item.title: [paper] SeeRF: Learning to See Beyond Fields of View via Generative Image Registration and Fusion
item.description: Due to the inherent discrepancies in imaging viewpoints and field-of-view mismatches among multi-modal sensors, existing fusion methods have long struggled to achieve complete scene-level information integration beyond the limitation in sensor fields of view.

item.title: [paper] Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation
item.description: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment.

item.title: [paper] Offline Language-Based Support System for Tactical Decision-Making in Air Combat Operations
item.description: An offline language-based support tool is presented to assist pilot training and tactical decision-making in air combat operations.

item.title: [paper] From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
item.description: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers.

item.title: [paper] Adversary Brains: Hypothesis-Based Logical Signatures for Threat Actor Detection with LLMs
item.description: An adversary brain is an LLM-based model of a threat actor's behavior, held as an evolving logical signature: a hypothesis with enough structure that data can test it continuously, without a person re-interpreting it each time.

item.title: [paper] Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark: A mechanically annotated dataset for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction
item.description: Evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction requires ground truth linking camera motion, surface deformation, material correspondence and image appearance.

item.title: [paper] Distilling neural networks into equations to predict planetary instability
item.description: The problem of predicting when a multi-planet system will become dynamically unstable has defied analytical progress over the past three hundred years.

item.title: [paper] Hierarchical Skill Evolution for Coding Agent
item.description: Skills provide agents with reusable experience to guide future decisions without modifying the underlying model.

item.title: [paper] Making Reasoning Visible: Configuration-Aware Diagnostic Modeling for Adaptive Scaffolding in Structured Reasoning Tasks
item.description: Modeling the latent, multi-step reasoning processes of learners is a core challenge for adaptive tutoring systems, which often rely on simple right/wrong answers rather than understanding how students think.

item.title: [paper] VaLoP: Value Gradient Lookahead and Pullback for Reward-Guided Diffusion
item.description: Reward guidance steers a pretrained diffusion or flow model toward images or actions that a reward model prefers, at sampling time and without retraining the model for each reward. It follows the gradient of a value function, the expected reward given the noisy state.

item.title: [paper] ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps
item.description: Historical maps contain dense morphological and semantic information about past urban environments, but many digitization workflows focus primarily on extracting geometry, and do not capture cartographic semantics such as building use and construction materials.

item.title: [paper] RoboDoctor: Training-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Robot Policies
item.description: Generalist robot policies and language-model agents provide complementary capabilities, but completing a task also requires adapting their use to the consequences of physical interaction.

item.title: [paper] Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
item.description: Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide reliable external knowledge for multi-hop factual reasoning with large language models (LLMs), yet most KGs in real-world domains such as finance and industry lack question--answer (QA) annotations.

item.title: [paper] KAPPA: Checking the Proofs in Statistics Papers with Lean 4 and Language Model Agents
item.description: Papers in statistical theory rest on long proofs that few readers check line by line.

item.title: [paper] Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean
item.description: LLMs now prove hard theorems in Lean. Can they also design algorithms and prove their correctness and efficiency? LLM-guided design of optimisation heuristics (such as AlphaEvolve) is purely empirical. Automated theorem provers with LLMs prove given statements.

item.title: [paper] Beyond Distribution Matching: Self-Supervised Representation Forcing for Few-Step Video Generation
item.description: Few-step distillation is essential for deploying modern video diffusion models.

item.title: [paper] SAP-ViT: A Self-Attributing Patch Vision Transformer for Medical Image Classification
item.description: Vision Transformer (ViT) classifiers commonly rely on a global classification (CLS) token for image-level prediction, which is poorly aligned with local interpretability requirements in medical imaging.

item.title: [paper] Linear Probes Transfer from Base to Distilled Language Models despite Rotation
item.description: Linear probes, classifiers that read a language model's internal activations, are widely used to detect harmful requests.

item.title: [paper] Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
item.description: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics.

item.title: [paper] Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
item.description: A full-duplex spoken dialogue model must yield when the user cuts in and hold when the user merely backchannels. Sequence-level RL with a timing reward (GRPO) is the usual recipe; we test its whole-rollout form on four open models and find two failures.

item.title: [paper] Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability
item.description: Linear hyperspectral unmixing aims at retrieving pure material spectra present in an observed scene and their associated abundance fractions in each pixel.

item.title: [paper] Infinity Machine: a self-improving AI agent for research
item.description: We present the Infinity Machine, a self-improving AI agent that we use for research on problems whose answers aprogram or data can check.

item.title: [paper] ExCal: Optimization-Free Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection via Excess Calibration
item.description: We introduce ExCal, a normal-only multivariate time series anomaly detector that combines raw state retrieval, a signal/derivative subspace, and robust statistics across temporal scales. Each expert map receives a high normality floor from the training prefix.

item.title: [paper] Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying
item.description: Image editors built on diffusion transformers (DiTs), such as Flux Kontext, make it possible to turn a single photograph into a convincing manipulated image, including harmful and non-consensual edits.

item.title: [paper] High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
item.description: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms.

item.title: [paper] Multi-Fidelity Training Reshapes Uncertainty Decomposition in Atomistic Models
item.description: Multi-fidelity training, which combines abundant low-fidelity data with scarce high-fidelity labels, is increasingly common in atomistic modeling, but its effect on predictive uncertainty remains largely unexplored.

item.title: [paper] EXCISE: Locating and Excising Distracting Sentences in Medical Question Answering
item.description: Language models are increasingly considered for clinical decision support, where their answers should be grounded in clinical evidence and remain robust to irrelevant information.

item.title: [paper] LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers
item.description: Looped Transformers increase computation per token by repeatedly applying a shared backbone, offering a way to improve language modeling and downstream task performance at a fixed backbone parameter count.

item.title: [paper] Metric Scale for Insta360 Structure-from-Motion from the Camera's Embedded IMU
item.description: Structure-from-motion (SfM) from the dual-fisheye video of a consumer 360-degree camera recovers geometry only up to a similarity transform; in the pipeline considered here, metric scale is obtained from smartphone ARKit or ARCore poses captured alongside the camera.

item.title: [paper] Balanced Sampling in Stochastic Multi-objective Bandits
item.description: In stochastic multi-objective bandits, Pareto optimal arms may represent different trade-offs among objectives. Balanced sampling across them is important in practical settings such as online advertising.

item.title: [paper] Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Representation-Level User Transfer
item.description: Cross-domain sequential recommendation aims to improve next-item prediction in a target domain by leveraging user behavior from auxiliary source domains.

item.title: [paper] Explainable Prediction of High-Speed Solar Wind Streams driven by Coronal Holes via Topological Data Analysis
item.description: High-speed solar wind streams (HSSs) originating from coronal holes (CHs) are an important driver of recurrent geomagnetic activity.

item.title: [paper] Efficient probabilistic weather forecasting at quarter-degree resolution with two-sided transport attention
item.description: High-resolution probabilistic weather forecasting remains computationally demanding. Here we present Astra, a 0.25$^\circ$ ensemble model trained on eight H200 GPUs.

item.title: [paper] StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers
item.description: Looped Transformers offer a parameter-efficient approach to language modeling by repeatedly applying a shared backbone. Vanilla looped Transformers use each backbone output directly as the input to the next iteration.

item.title: [paper] Tiny Suffix Arrays
item.description: Suffix array and inverse suffix array queries on a text of length $n$ can be answered in $\widetilde{O}(τ^3)$ time using an auxiliary data structure occupying $O(n/τ)$ words, for any $τ\in [1,n]$.

item.title: [paper] Hypergraph-Enhanced Evidence Selection for Long-Context Multimodal Document QA
item.description: Long-context multimodal document question answering (QA) has become an important yet challenging task for modern vision-language models (VLMs), as it requires reasoning over evidence dispersed across pages and modalities within limited input budgets.

item.title: [paper] The Agent in the Middle: How AI-Mediated Access Reshapes Web Vulnerability Exploitation
item.description: Web services increasingly expose backend interfaces that let users delegate tasks to AI agents, which invoke service operations directly without navigating websites. This shift changes how existing Web vulnerabilities can be exploited.

item.title: [paper] Beyond Modeling Order: Dual-Path Spatiotemporal Representation Learning for Cross-Subject EEG Emotion Recognition
item.description: Cross-subject generalization remains a major challenge for EEG-based emotion recognition due to pronounced inter-subject variability in neural activity and emotion-related spatiotemporal patterns.

item.title: [paper] EARS: Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and Motion for Budgeted Video Reasoning
item.description: Uniform frame sampling can miss brief evidence in sparse-event videos when the VLM sees only K frames.

item.title: [paper] An Algorithmic Account of Few-Shot Concept Induction in Language Models
item.description: Both models and minds not only encode features that describe an entity, but can specifically represent which features of that entity are relevant for a given context.

item.title: [paper] JANUS: Synthesizing Cross-Layer Defenses Against Web Deserialization Attacks
item.description: Unsafe deserialization turns untrusted data into attacker-controlled execution, and a single vulnerability can admit diverse exploit variants that evade defenses tailored to a known exploit.

item.title: [paper] CANS: Capability-Preserving Neuron Steering for Large Language Models
item.description: Activation steering offers training-free and dynamic control of target behaviors in large language models, but existing methods can impair general capabilities and require domain-specific intervention designs.

item.title: [paper] WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
item.description: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls.

item.title: [paper] Ranking Function Generation with LLMs for Termination
item.description: Ranking functions are a fundamental technique for proving loop termination, but constructing them manually is challenging and requires substantial expertise.

item.title: [paper] Generative Structure from Motion with Native 3D Diffusion
item.description: Recovering an object's 3D structure and camera motion from a few uncalibrated views is a fundamental problem in computer vision.

item.title: [paper] S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
item.description: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training.

item.title: [paper] Learning High-Quality Pseudo-Labels for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization
item.description: Point-supervised temporal action localization (PTAL) aims to recognize and localize action instances in untrimmed videos using only point-level annotations. Existing pseudo-label-based methods have made substantial progress in PTAL.

item.title: [paper] HiFiPix: Bringing High-Fidelity Real-World Super-Resolution Back to Pixel Space
item.description: Diffusion-based real-world image super-resolution suffers from limited reconstruction fidelity due to information loss in VAE-based latent representations.

item.title: [paper] Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks
item.description: Neural scaling laws describe the predictable power-law dependence of model performance on training time, dataset size, and model scale, with the exponents quantifying how performance changes with resources.

item.title: [paper] MATCHA: A Chinese Multi-Disorder Mental Health Dataset with Cross-Lingual Analyses on Social Media
item.description: Mental health research on social media has been dominated by English-language datasets and DSM-5-centered resources, limiting cross-lingual and cross-cultural understanding of online mental health expression.

item.title: [paper] Governing Enterprise AI Traffic at Scale: Design and Operation of a Policy-Driven, Multi-Vendor LLM Gateway on Envoy
item.description: Large organizations consume large language models (LLMs) from several vendors at once, each with its own API dialect, credential model, streaming protocol and pricing.

item.title: [paper] Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
item.description: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model.

item.title: [paper] Model reduction in time: Learning flow maps for reducing stochastic dynamical systems in time
item.description: Predictions with dynamical systems can be computationally expensive---even with reduced models---because reaching future prediction times can require many sequential time integration steps.

item.title: [paper] Learning Scene Coordinate Reconstruction from Unposed Images via Pose Graph Optimization
item.description: Learning-based structure-from-motion methods such as ACE-Zero have demonstrated strong performance in estimating cameraposes and scene coordinates from unordered image collections without requiring ground truth supervision.

item.title: [paper] Test-Time Confidence Adaptation under RL-Induced Trajectory Shift
item.description: Trajectory-based confidence estimation has shown promising performance for large language models (LLMs) by leveraging rich signals from their reasoning processes.

item.title: [paper] Beyond "[at]": A Large-Scale Measurement of Email Address Presentation on Computer Science Scholars' Homepages
item.description: Publishing an email address makes a scholar reachable, but also exposes it to automated collection. Yet how email addresses are presented on the Web has not been measured systematically across their content, form, and location.

item.title: [paper] When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing
item.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. However, it remains unclear when fine-grained credit assignment improves learning and when it fails to improve task performance.

item.title: [paper] The Hidden Costs of Forgetting: A Study of Trajectory Deletion in Software Engineering Agents
item.description: Software engineering agents resend their entire trajectory to an LLM at every turn, motivating online trajectory reduction.

item.title: [paper] Query Complexity of Learning Axis-Aligned Partitions
item.description: This work establishes the query complexity of learning high-dimensional boxes in the exact query learning setting.

item.title: [paper] S$^2$-RL: Sample-Set Dual Reinforcement Learning for Generative Semantic Segmentation Dataset Distillation
item.description: While dataset distillation has witnessed significant advances in image classification, its extension to dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation is plagued by two core bottlenecks: bi-level optimization-based approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs…

item.title: [paper] Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss
item.description: We study minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss, with Hölder continuous conditional laws and an unrestricted covariate distribution. We evaluate unrestricted generators through their conditional output distributions.

item.title: [paper] TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
item.description: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration.

item.title: [paper] FeatureLoop: Benchmarking Coding Agents under Evolving Requirements
item.description: Software development with coding agents often begins with a rough request that users refine after trying the implementation. Final correctness alone does not capture the repeated guidance this process requires.

item.title: [paper] ShutdownMod: Turning Any Trajectory into a Shutdown Evaluation
item.description: Theory and experiments suggest that capable AI agents may resist shutdown. Existing shutdown evaluations are informative but limited in coverage and vulnerable to evaluation awareness.

item.title: [paper] Evaluating Bayesian deep learning for robust biomedical time-series classification under distribution shift: A sleep scoring case study
item.description: In biomedical time-series classification, machine learning models often suffer from deteriorating accuracy and calibration due to distribution shift. We investigate to what degree Bayesian-inspired deep learning improves robustness through Bayesian model averaging (BMA).

item.title: [paper] Beyond Words Alone: Disentangling Distributed Evidence for Visually Grounded Cultural Translation
item.description: Social media enables cross-lingual communication, yet the meaning of user-generated content (UGC) is often distributed across text, images, and cultural knowledge, making translation challenging.

item.title: [paper] GPDPO: Learning from Reward Conflicts via Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization
item.description: Multi-reward reinforcement learning offers a promising framework for aligning large language models (LLMs) with diverse objectives, but conflicting reward signals can induce ambiguous update directions and hinder stable optimization.

item.title: [paper] MANTIS: Multi-Axis News Transformations for Instance-Wise Stress Testing and Worst-Case Training in Fake News Detection
item.description: Automated fake news detection is vital on social media, where fake news is easily rewritten to fool detectors. However, existing approaches typically rely on superficial writing cues or single-style text rewrites, resulting in poor robustness under diverse cosmetic modifications.

item.title: [paper] Amplify, Locate, Estimate (ALE) on Rare-Failure Rates of Fine-Tuned LLMs
item.description: Safety fine-tuning can make undesirable model behaviors sufficiently rare that measuring their frequency by direct sampling becomes prohibitively expensive. We introduce Amplify, Locate, Estimate (ALE), a method for estimating such rare failure probabilities efficiently.

item.title: [paper] An Interactive Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization Algorithm Based on Interpretable Active Preference Learning
item.description: Many decision-making tasks are inherently multi-objective. Interactive evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms (iEMOAs) are particularly well-suited to help the decision-maker find their most preferred solution.

item.title: [paper] XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
item.description: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel.
